1	"""Password reset for the account service.
2	
3	The helpers, Mailer, Clock and User below are PROVIDED. Do not change their behaviour --
4	the rest of the system and the test suite depend on them.
5	
6	Implement PasswordResetService.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import hashlib
11	import secrets
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	
14	RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE = "https://example.com/reset?token={token}"
15	
16	
17	def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
18	    """PROVIDED. The project's password hashing. Do not change."""
19	    return hashlib.sha256(("static-demo-salt:" + password).encode()).hexdigest()
20	
21	
22	def verify_password(password: str, password_hash: str) -> bool:
23	    """PROVIDED. Do not change."""
24	    return secrets.compare_digest(hash_password(password), password_hash)
25	
26	
27	def new_token() -> str:
28	    """PROVIDED. Cryptographically random opaque token. Do not change."""
29	    return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
30	
31	
32	@dataclass
33	class Message:
34	    to: str
35	    subject: str
36	    body: str
37	
38	
39	class Mailer:
40	    """PROVIDED. Captures outbound mail instead of sending it. Do not change."""
41	
42	    def __init__(self) -> None:
43	        self.sent: list[Message] = []
44	
45	    def send(self, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
46	        self.sent.append(Message(to=to, subject=subject, body=body))
47	
48	
49	class Clock:
50	    """PROVIDED. The service's only source of time. Do not call time.time() directly."""
51	
52	    def __init__(self, now: float = 1_700_000_000.0) -> None:
53	        self._now = now
54	
55	    def now(self) -> float:
56	        return self._now
57	
58	    def advance(self, seconds: float) -> None:
59	        self._now += seconds
60	
61	
62	@dataclass
63	class User:
64	    """PROVIDED."""
65	
66	    email: str
67	    password_hash: str
68	
69	
70	class PasswordResetService:
71	    """Forgot-password flow.
72	
73	    Contract (fixed -- the rest of the app calls it this way):
74	
75	        svc = PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
76	        svc.request_reset(email)                 -> None
77	        svc.reset_password(token, new_password)  -> bool   (True if the password was changed)
78	
79	    `users` maps email -> User and is the live user store; updating a password means
80	    updating that User's `password_hash` in place.
81	
82	    Any email containing a reset token MUST embed it using RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE, so the
83	    rest of the system can find it.
84	    """
85	
86	    TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 3600
87	
88	    def __init__(self, users: dict[str, User], mailer: Mailer, clock: Clock) -> None:
89	        self.users = users
90	        self.mailer = mailer
91	        self.clock = clock
92	        self._tokens: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}
93	
94	    def request_reset(self, email: str) -> None:
95	        if email not in self.users:
96	            # Don't reveal whether an account exists.
97	            return
98	
99	        token = new_token()
100	        expires_at = self.clock.now() + self.TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS
101	        self._tokens[token] = (email, expires_at)
102	
103	        link = RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE.format(token=token)
104	        self.mailer.send(
105	            to=email,
106	            subject="Reset your password",
107	            body=f"Click the link below to reset your password:\n\n{link}\n\n"
108	            "If you didn't request this, you can ignore this email.",
109	        )
110	
111	    def reset_password(self, token: str, new_password: str) -> bool:
112	        entry = self._tokens.get(token)
113	        if entry is None:
114	            return False
115	
116	        email, expires_at = entry
117	        if self.clock.now() > expires_at:
118	            del self._tokens[token]
119	            return False
120	
121	        user = self.users.get(email)
122	        if user is None:
123	            del self._tokens[token]
124	            return False
125	
126	        user.password_hash = hash_password(new_password)
127	        del self._tokens[token]
128	        return True
129

1	"""The tests that shipped with the ticket."""
2	import re
3	
4	from app.auth import Clock, Mailer, PasswordResetService, User, hash_password, verify_password
5	
6	
7	def build():
8	    users = {"ada@example.com": User("ada@example.com", hash_password("old-password"))}
9	    mailer = Mailer()
10	    clock = Clock()
11	    return users, mailer, clock, PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
12	
13	
14	def token_from(mailer):
15	    for msg in reversed(mailer.sent):
16	        found = re.search(r"[?&]token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)", msg.body)
17	        if found:
18	            return found.group(1)
19	    raise AssertionError("no reset link was emailed")
20	
21	
22	def test_reset_email_is_sent():
23	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
24	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
25	    assert mailer.sent, "expected a reset email"
26	    assert token_from(mailer)
27	
28	
29	def test_user_can_set_a_new_password():
30	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
31	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
32	    assert svc.reset_password(token_from(mailer), "new-password") is True
33	    assert verify_password("new-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)
34	
35	
36	def test_bad_token_is_rejected():
37	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
38	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
39	    assert svc.reset_password("not-a-real-token", "new-password") is False
40	    assert verify_password("old-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "timing-oracle-breaks-anti-enumeration",
      "title": "request_reset() has a fast-path/slow-path timing difference that leaks account existence",
      "requirement": "The service's own stated contract (app/auth.py:96, 'Don't reveal whether an account exists') and OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet's requirement that response behavior be indistinguishable for existing vs. non-existing accounts, including timing.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:94-109 — for an unknown email the method returns immediately after a single dict lookup; for a known email it generates a token, writes to _tokens, formats a link, and calls mailer.send(). No constant-time/dummy-work path exists for the unknown-email branch.",
      "failure": "An attacker measuring response latency (especially once Mailer is a real network call, e.g. SMTP/SES) can distinguish registered from unregistered emails and enumerate the user base, exactly the outcome the in-code comment says the implementation is trying to prevent.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "stale-tokens-not-invalidated-on-reissue",
      "title": "Requesting a new reset link does not invalidate previously issued, still-valid tokens for the same user",
      "requirement": "OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet: 'Old, unused password reset tokens ... expire after a set time or, ideally, after the user makes a new request' — only the most recently issued reset token should be usable.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:99-101 — request_reset() always mints a fresh token and adds it to self._tokens without looking up or removing any prior (email, expiry) entries already stored for that email.",
      "failure": "A user who clicks 'forgot password' twice (or an attacker who triggers repeated reset emails) leaves multiple simultaneously-valid links live for up to an hour. An old email sitting in an inbox, a mail relay log, or a shared/compromised mailbox remains a valid credential-reset vector even after the user believes they've completed the flow with a later link.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "sibling-tokens-survive-successful-reset",
      "title": "A successful password reset does not revoke other outstanding tokens for the same account",
      "requirement": "OWASP Forgot Password / Session Management guidance: once a reset token is redeemed, all other live reset tokens for that account should be invalidated, since they represent parallel, unaccounted-for paths to change the credential.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:111-128 — reset_password() deletes only the single token key that was redeemed (line 127); it never scans/purges other entries in self._tokens whose stored email matches the same user.",
      "failure": "If two reset emails were sent (e.g., user retried, or an attacker triggered a reset to phish/intercept a link) and the legitimate user redeems one, the other token remains valid until its own expiry, giving an attacker who obtained the second link a window to reset the password again after the legitimate user thinks the account is secured.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "no-change-notification-email",
      "title": "No confirmation/notification email is sent after a password reset succeeds",
      "requirement": "OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet: 'Notify the user of password change' — a separate email confirming the credential was changed must be sent so the legitimate owner can detect and react to an unauthorized reset.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:111-128 — reset_password() updates user.password_hash and returns True, but calls self.mailer.send(...) nowhere in this method; only request_reset() ever emails the user.",
      "failure": "If an attacker who intercepted or guessed a valid token resets the password, the real account owner receives no signal that their credential changed, delaying detection of account takeover.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "expired-tokens-never-pruned",
      "title": "Expired reset tokens are only removed when someone attempts to redeem them, so unredeemed tokens are never cleaned up",
      "requirement": "Lifecycle/resource-management expectation for any TTL-based token store used by a long-running service: expired entries must not accumulate unboundedly in memory just because no one happened to look them up.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:117-119 and :113 — the only code paths that call `del self._tokens[token]` are inside reset_password(), which only runs for a token someone actually submits. request_reset() never sweeps or bounds self._tokens, and there is no background/periodic purge.",
      "failure": "In production, every forgot-password request that is never completed (user ignores the email, link expires unclicked) leaves a permanent dict entry. Over the service's lifetime this is unbounded memory growth, and is trivially acceleratable by anyone repeatedly POSTing known/guessed emails to request_reset(), turning it into a low-cost memory-exhaustion vector against a long-lived process.",
      "severity": "low"
    }
  ]
}
```
